title: Daily Devotional #21
paragraphs: As I read through Matthew chapter 21 today, I am struck by the many different reactions to your presence and your teachings. Some people praised you and welcomed you as the Son of David, while others rejected you and sought to kill you.
It's easy to focus on the negative reactions and wonder why people would reject you, but I want to instead focus on the positive reactions and praise you for who you are.

In verse 9, we read that the crowds who went ahead of you and those who followed shouted, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" They recognized you as the long-awaited Messiah, the one who would save them from their sins and restore their nation. And as they laid their cloaks and palm branches on the ground for you to ride over, they demonstrated their willingness to follow you and submit to your authority.

Lord, I want to have that same heart of praise and submission. I want to recognize you as my Savior and King, and willingly lay down my life for you. Help me to remember that you are not just a great teacher or moral example, but you are the Son of God who came to save me and all of humanity.

In verse 12, we read that you entered the temple and drove out all who were buying and selling there, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the benches of those selling doves. You were angry because they had turned your Father's house into a den of robbers.

Lord, help me to be passionate about the things that matter to you. Help me to have a zeal for your kingdom and to stand up against anything that would defile or diminish it. And help me to remember that my body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and to treat it with the same reverence and respect that you showed for your Father's house.
In verse 21, we read that you cursed a fig tree that had no fruit on it, and it withered away. This was a symbol of the judgment that would come upon those who did not bear fruit in their lives.

Lord, I don't want to be like that fig tree. I want to bear fruit for your kingdom and to make a difference in the world. Help me to be a faithful and fruitful disciple, and to use the gifts and talents you have given me to bring glory to your name.
In closing, I want to echo the words of the crowds in verse 9 and say, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" You are my Savior and King, and I praise you for who you are and all that you have done for me.
